overview: Index ek extra file hai jo search fast karti hai. Types: primary (ordering key), clustering (ordering non-key), secondary (non-ordering); dense vs sparse; multilevel. GATE me mostly block-count / levels ki numerical aur clustered/dense/sparse concepts aate hain.
whyItMatters: 15 PYQs, 1989-2026; 2020-2026 me har saal ek NAT ya concept question.
coreConcept: Index entries chhoti hoti hain (key + pointer), isliye index ke blocks data ke blocks se kam hote hain; multilevel index binary search ko log base bf tak le aata hai.
hinglishExplanation: Pehle blocking factor nikaalo: records per block = floor(B / R). Data blocks = ceil(N / bf). Dense index me har record ki entry, sparse me har block ki entry. Index entry size = key + block pointer, isse index blocking factor aur index ke blocks nikalte hain. Multilevel me tab tak levels banate ho jab tak top level 1 block me na aa jaye.
formalDefinition: Blocking factor bf = floor(B / R). Index entries per block fi = floor(B / (K + P)). Levels: ceil(log_fi(entries)).
importantProperties: Primary index: ordered file + key field, sparse (block anchor).
Clustering index: ordered file par non-key field.
Secondary index: unordered field par, dense hona zaroori.
Dense index: har search key value ki entry; sparse: har block ki entry.
Sparse index sirf ordered file par ban sakta hai.
Ek file par ek hi primary/clustering index (kyunki ordering ek hi), kai secondary ho sakte hain.
Clustered index: data records ka order index entries ke order jaisa.
Hash index: equality search ke liye, range/ordered scan ke liye nahi; dense hoti hai.
Multilevel index me first level ke baad next levels first-level blocks ka sparse index hote hain.

formulas.levels: smallest L such that fi^L >= entries

keyPropertiesAndIdentities: Single-level sparse index blocks = ceil(data blocks / fi).
Binary search on index cost = ceil(log2(index blocks)) + 1.
commonPitfalls: Dense/sparse ka data blocks ya records se count galat lena.
Clustered aur primary ko same maan lena.
Unspanned organization me bf ko floor karna bhoolna.
standardTechniques: bf -> data blocks -> index entries per block -> index blocks ki chain me calculate karo.
Access cost = index levels + 1 data block.
